function.name: recipe_search_find
function.description: Locate recipes based on the type of dish. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

dish.description: The name of the dish to search for.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find chicken soup noodle recipes and vegan salad recipes. We have a tool `recipe_search_find` which can locate recipes based on dish type. It accepts parameters: dish (string), diet optional with values Vegan, Vegetarian, Paleo, Keto; default Keto.

We need two searches:

1) Chicken soup noodles - presumably not vegan or vegetarian? It's likely regular chicken soup noodle recipe. So we call with dish="chicken soup noodles". No dietary preference needed unless they want something else. But maybe they'd like standard recipe. We'll just use default diet=Keto? That might produce keto-friendly version but it's okay. Or we could omit diet param entirely so it defaults to Keto. However if they didn't specify diet, perhaps better to leave unspecified. But the function signature requires at least dish. Diet is optional. If omitted, default will apply. Let's do first call without specifying diet.

2) Purely vegan salad recipe. They said "purevegan salad" meaning purely vegan. So set diet="Vegan".

Thus we'll make two calls sequentially using the tool. Then return results. Probably combine them into one response listing both sets of recipes. Use markdown formatting. Provide links etc. Since no other instructions, proceed accordingly.
